examples.japanese: {川岸|かわぎし}に{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: I sat down on the riverbank.

examples.japanese: {川岸|かわぎし}に{桜|さくら}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Cherry trees are lined up along the riverbank.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{川岸|かわぎし}で{石|いし}を{投|な}げて{遊|あそ}んでいた。
examples.english: The children were playing on the riverbank, throwing stones.

notes:
Refers to the edge or bank of a river. A straightforward compound of {川|かわ} (river) and {岸|きし} (shore/bank), with the second element voiced ({岸|ぎし}) due to rendaku.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {川岸|かわぎし}に{立|た}つ: to stand on the riverbank
- {川岸|かわぎし}を{歩|ある}く: to walk along the riverbank
- {川岸|かわぎし}の{草|くさ}: grass on the riverbank

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {河岸|かし}: riverbank — also read かし, often refers to a wharf or fish market (as in {河岸|かし}を{変|か}える, to move to a different bar/restaurant)
- {川辺|かわべ}: riverside — emphasizes the area near the river rather than the bank itself
- {岸辺|きしべ}: shore, waterside — can refer to any body of water, not just rivers
